title_en: Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Activities of Overseas Non-Governmental Organizations within the Territory of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purpose of regulating and guiding the activities of overseas non-governmental organizations within the territory of China, protecting their lawful rights and interests, and promoting exchange and cooperation.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to the activities conducted by overseas non-governmental organizations within the territory of China.
For the purposes of this Law, overseas non-governmental organizations mean non-profit and non-governmental social organizations such as foundations, social groups, and think tanks that are lawfully established outside the territory of China.

Article 3 Overseas non-governmental organizations may, in accordance with this Law, conduct activities that are conducive to the development of public welfare undertakings in such fields as economy, education, science and technology, culture, health, sports, environmental protection, and in such aspects as poverty relief and disaster relief.
Article 4 Overseas non-governmental organizations that conduct activities within the territory of China according to law shall be protected by law.

Article 5 An overseas non-governmental organization shall abide by Chinese laws when conducting activities within the territory of China, and shall not endanger China's national unity, security and ethnic solidarity, and shall not damage China's national interests, social public interests, and the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons and other organizations.
An overseas non-governmental organization shall not engage in or sponsor for-profit activities or political activities within the territory of China, and shall not illegally engage in or sponsor religious activities.

Article 6 The public security department of the State Council and the public security organs of the people's governments at the provincial level shall be the registration management authorities for the activities of overseas non-governmental organizations within the territory of China.
The relevant departments and units of the State Council and the relevant departments and units of the people's governments at the provincial level shall be the corresponding business supervisory units for the activities of overseas non-governmental organizations within the territory of China.

Article 7 The public security organs of the people's governments at or above the county level and the relevant departments shall, within their respective functions and duties, supervise and administer the activities of overseas non-governmental organizations within the territory of China according to law and provide services.
The State shall establish a coordination mechanism for the supervision and administration of overseas non-governmental organizations, which shall be responsible for studying, coordinating and resolving major issues in the supervision, administration and service facilitation of the activities of overseas non-governmental organizations within the territory of China.
Article 8 The State shall give commendation to overseas non-governmental organizations that have made outstanding contributions to the development of China's public welfare undertakings.

Article 9 An overseas non-governmental organization that conducts activities within the territory of China shall register and establish a representative office according to law; where it needs to conduct temporary activities within the territory of China without registering and establishing a representative office, it shall file for the record according to law.
An overseas non-governmental organization that has not registered and established a representative office or whose temporary activities have not been filed for the record shall not conduct or conduct in disguised form activities within the territory of China, and shall not entrust, finance or entrust in disguised form, or finance in disguised form any unit or individual within the territory of China to conduct activities within the territory of China.

Article 11 An overseas non-governmental organization that applies to register and establish a representative office shall obtain the consent of the business supervisory unit.
The list of business supervisory units shall be published by the public security department of the State Council and the public security organs of the people's governments at the provincial level, in conjunction with the relevant departments.

Article 14 Where a representative office of an overseas non-governmental organization needs to alter the registered items, it shall, within thirty days from the date of consent by the business supervisory unit, apply to the registration management authority for alteration registration.

Article 16 Where an overseas non-governmental organization that has not established a representative office within the territory of China conducts temporary activities within the territory of China, it shall cooperate with State organs, people's organizations, public institutions, or social organizations of China (hereinafter referred to as Chinese partner units).

Article 18 A representative office of an overseas non-governmental organization shall conduct activities under its registered name, within the registered business scope and activity region.
An overseas non-governmental organization shall not establish branch offices within the territory of China, unless otherwise provided by the State Council.

Article 19 A representative office of an overseas non-governmental organization shall, before December 31 each year, submit the activity plan for the following year containing contents such as project implementation and fund utilization to the business supervisory unit, and within ten days after obtaining the consent of the business supervisory unit, file it with the registration management authority for the record. Where the activity plan needs to be adjusted under special circumstances, it shall promptly file the adjustment with the registration management authority for the record.

Article 20 An overseas non-governmental organization conducting activities within the territory of China shall not attach any conditions to the Chinese partner units or beneficiaries that violate Chinese laws and regulations.

Article 21 The funds for the activities of an overseas non-governmental organization within the territory of China shall include:
(1) Funds from lawful sources outside the territory of China;
(2) Interest on bank deposits within the territory of China; and
(3) Other funds lawfully obtained within the territory of China.
An overseas non-governmental organization shall not obtain or use funds other than those specified in the preceding paragraph for its activities within the territory of China.
An overseas non-governmental organization and its representative office shall not conduct fundraising within the territory of China.

Article 22 An overseas non-governmental organization that has established a representative office shall manage the funds used within the territory of China through the bank account of the representative office that has been filed with the registration management authority for the record.
An overseas non-governmental organization conducting temporary activities shall manage the funds used within the territory of China through the bank account of the Chinese partner unit, and shall practice separate accounting and use the funds exclusively for designated purposes.
Without the bank accounts specified in the preceding two paragraphs, the overseas non-governmental organization, Chinese partner unit or individual shall not receive or disburse funds for project activities within the territory of China in any other form.

Article 23 An overseas non-governmental organization shall use the funds in accordance with the registered business scope and activity region of the representative office or the agreement with the Chinese partner unit.

Article 24 A representative office of an overseas non-governmental organization shall implement the unified accounting system of China. The financial accounting report shall be audited by an accounting firm within the territory of China.

Article 25 An overseas non-governmental organization conducting activities within the territory of China shall handle foreign exchange receipts and disbursements in accordance with the provisions of China on foreign exchange control.
Article 26 A representative office of an overseas non-governmental organization shall undergo tax registration, tax declaration and tax payment according to law.

Article 27 A representative office of an overseas non-governmental organization shall comply with laws and administrative regulations when employing staff within the territory of China, and shall report the information on the employed staff to the business supervisory unit and the registration management authority for the record.

Article 28 A representative office of an overseas non-governmental organization or an overseas non-governmental organization conducting temporary activities shall not recruit members within the territory of China, unless otherwise provided by the State Council.

Article 30 An overseas non-governmental organization conducting temporary activities shall conduct its activities under the name that has been filed for the record.
The overseas non-governmental organization and the Chinese partner unit shall, within thirty days after the conclusion of the temporary activities, submit a written report on the activities and fund utilization to the registration management authority.

Article 31 A representative office of an overseas non-governmental organization shall, before January 31 each year, submit the work report for the preceding year to the business supervisory unit. After the business supervisory unit issues its opinion, the report shall be submitted to the registration management authority before March 31 for annual inspection.
The annual work report shall include the audited financial accounting report, an overview of the activities conducted, and information on changes in personnel and organizational structure.
The representative office of an overseas non-governmental organization shall make the annual work report public on the unified website of the registration management authority.

Article 32 No unit or individual within the territory of China shall accept the entrustment or funding from an overseas non-governmental organization that has not registered a representative office or whose temporary activities have not been filed for the record, or act as an agent or act as an agent in disguised form for such an overseas non-governmental organization to conduct activities within the territory of China.

Article 33 The State guarantees and supports overseas non-governmental organizations in lawfully conducting activities within the territory of China. The relevant departments of the people's governments at all levels shall provide necessary convenience and services for overseas non-governmental organizations to lawfully conduct activities within the territory of China.

Article 34 The public security department of the State Council and the public security organs of the people's governments at the provincial level shall, in conjunction with the relevant departments, formulate the catalogue of activity fields and projects for overseas non-governmental organizations, publish the list of business supervisory units, and provide guidance for overseas non-governmental organizations in conducting activities.

Article 35 The relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall provide policy consultation and activity guidance services for overseas non-governmental organizations according to law.
The registration management authority shall, through a unified website, publish the procedures for overseas non-governmental organizations to apply for the establishment of representative offices and to file for temporary activities, for the reference of overseas non-governmental organizations.
Article 36 Representative offices of overseas non-governmental organizations shall enjoy tax preferences and other policies according to law.
Article 37 No fees shall be charged for the annual inspection of representative offices of overseas non-governmental organizations.

Article 38 The chief representative and the foreign representatives of a representative office of an overseas non-governmental organization may, by presenting the registration certificate and representative certification documents, handle employment and other work formalities according to law.

Article 39 Overseas non-governmental organizations conducting activities within the territory of China shall accept the supervision and administration of the public security organs, the relevant departments and the business supervisory units.

Article 40 The business supervisory unit shall be responsible for giving opinions on the establishment of representative offices, alteration of registered items, and annual work reports of overseas non-governmental organizations; guiding and supervising overseas non-governmental organizations and their representative offices to lawfully conduct activities; and assisting the public security organs and other departments in investigating and punishing the illegal acts of overseas non-governmental organizations and their representative offices.

Article 42 The public security organs may inquire into the bank accounts of the units and individuals related to the incident under investigation, and the relevant financial institutions and financial regulatory authorities shall cooperate. With respect to the funds in bank accounts suspected of involvement in illegal activities, with the approval of the person in charge of the public security organ of the people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts, the public security organs may request the People's Court to freeze the same according to law; with respect to the funds in bank accounts suspected of involvement in criminal activities, the freezing measures shall be taken in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 43 The departments of state security, foreign affairs, finance, financial supervision and administration, customs, taxation, and foreign experts shall, within their respective duties, exercise supervision and administration over overseas non-governmental organizations and their representative offices according to law.

Article 44 The anti-money laundering administrative department of the State Council shall, according to law, supervise and administer the compliance of representative offices of overseas non-governmental organizations, Chinese partner units, and units and individuals within the territory of China that receive funds from overseas non-governmental organizations with the laws and regulations on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing during the opening and use of bank accounts.

Article 48 Where an overseas non-governmental organization or its representative office is subject to cancellation of registration, revocation of the registration certificate, or the temporary activities are banned due to violation of the provisions of this Law, it shall not re-establish a representative office or conduct temporary activities within the territory of China within five years from the date of such cancellation, revocation or ban.
Where an overseas non-governmental organization conducts activities without having registered a representative office or without having filed temporary activities for the record, it shall not re-establish a representative office or conduct temporary activities within the territory of China within five years from the date on which the activities are banned.
An overseas non-governmental organization that falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 47 of this Law may be included in the list of unwelcome entities by the public security department of the State Council, and shall not re-establish a representative office or conduct temporary activities within the territory of China.

Article 49 Where a representative office of an overseas non-governmental organization is ordered to cease its activities within a specified time limit, the registration management authority shall seal up its registration certificate, seal and financial vouchers. Where the registration is cancelled or the registration certificate is revoked, the registration management authority shall confiscate its registration certificate and seal and announce their invalidation.

Article 50 Where any overseas personnel violate the provisions of this Law, the relevant authorities may order them to leave the country within a time limit, repatriate them, or deport them according to law.

Article 51 Where the public security organs, relevant departments, business supervisory units and their staff members, in the supervision and administration of overseas non-governmental organizations, fail to perform their duties, or abuse their powers, neglect their duties, or engage in malpractices for personal gain, they shall be investigated for legal liability according to law.

Article 52 Any violation of the provisions of this Law that constitutes a violation of public security administration shall be subject to public security administration punishment by the public security organ according to law; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 53 Where overseas schools, hospitals, research institutions or academic organizations in natural science and engineering technology conduct exchanges and cooperation with domestic schools, hospitals, research institutions or academic organizations in natural science and engineering technology, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.
Where the activities within the territory of China of the overseas schools, hospitals, institutions and organizations specified in the preceding paragraph violate the provisions of Article 5 of this Law, legal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Article 54 This Law shall come into force as of January 1, 2017.
